question: Using the START triage system, a patient at a mass-casualty incident is breathing at 28 breaths/min, has a radial pulse present, and is confused but follows simple commands. Which triage colour is correct?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Respiratory rate >30/min OR altered mental status with breathing present = Red (Immediate) in START. This patient meets the mental-status criterion even though RR is 28 — confused/not following commands = Immediate; however, 28 breaths/min alone (20–30 zone) combined with confusion also places this patient in Red.
Yellow requires: breathing present, RR ≤30, radial pulse present, and able to follow commands. This patient is confused and not fully following commands, so Yellow is incorrect.
Green (walking wounded) applies to ambulatory patients with minor injuries. This patient has an altered level of consciousness and is not ambulatory in the scenario.
Black applies to patients not breathing after airway repositioning (deceased) or clearly non-survivable injuries with overwhelming demand on resources. This patient is breathing and has a pulse.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the START algorithm: first check breathing (open airway if needed), then RR >30 = Red, then radial pulse absent = Red, then unable to follow simple commands = Red. Any other breathing patient = Yellow.

Well done. In START, any altered mental status (unable to follow commands) with breathing present = Red. Memorise the algorithm: breathe? → rate >30? → no radial pulse? → no commands? → each 'yes' = Immediate.
